text:
Maggie L: quick question — our current request/response logging stores full bodies for sampled traces. ops is worried about attachments and PII leaking into S3. can we steer towards field-level hide-and-hash earlier in the pipeline?
Rajeev: +1, but need to balance debuggability. if we hash too early we lose ability to inspect error payloads. maybe keep a short TTL raw store gated by a breakglass flow? :thinking:
Dan: I don't love long TTLs. ops already complains about retention. proposal: per-route minimal-raw-ttl (e.g. 15m) + immediate redaction of known sensitive fields (ssn,credit_card,email) before writing to durable logs. keep HMACs for dedupe.
Emily: can we do per-customer routing? some customers (enterprise) require zero raw retention, others want full traces for debugging. console UX should show when a trace is 'sanitized' vs 'raw available (time-limited)'.
Maggie L: agreed — UX needs to be explicit. also want a telemetry flag so billing/latency dashboards note when samples were scrubbed. otherwise SLA analysis is noisy.
Rajeev: technical sketch: run a small early filter service that parses request/response and emits two outputs: 1) sanitized record -> long-term telemetry store 2) raw blob -> short TTL bucket with access controlled by audit token. add HMAC field for PII values into sanitized record.
Dan: pseudo-config we could add to routes.yaml: ```yaml
routes:
  - id: /v2/generate
    sampling: 0.01
    raw_ttl_secs: 900  # 15m
    redact_fields: ["email","ssn","card_number"]
    allow_raw_unmask: ["oncall","audit"]
```
Emily: love the config. question: how do we handle embeddings outputs? PII could be encoded in vectors. hashing doesn't help. need a classifier before embedding to detect PII and either ban/strip or mark trace as sensitive.
Maggie L: we should add a 'vector_sensitive' flag from the preprocessor. if true, drop raw and only keep vector fingerprint/HMAC. also surface this in the console per-sample.
Rajeev: ops implications: more CPU at ingress for classifiers, but cheaper than incident remediation. think we can reuse our existing tiny classifier service (cpu-bound). need to add quota exemption for classification bursts.
ops-bot: note created: /policies/logging-field-hiding (draft) — reviewers: @Rajeev @Maggie L @Dan. Link: https://redwood.internal/policies/LOG-FIELD-HIDE-2
Dan: UX nuance — rollout plan: default to keep current behavior behind a feature-flag, enable per-tenant opt-in via console, then flip global default after 4 weeks of telemetry. we need console banner & changelog item.
Emily: also add clear audit logs whenever someone uses "allow_raw_unmask". legal will want an immutable trail.
Maggie L: +1. can we add a short sample view in console that shows sanitized vs raw TTL and a 'request redaction map' (which fields were redacted/hmaced)?
Rajeev: implementation tasks: 1) ingress filter service change 2) small schema addition to telemetry (redaction_map, vector_sensitive) 3) console indicator + audit logs 4) per-route config + rollout flag. I can pick up 1 and 2 this sprint.
Dan: I'll draft rollout steps and the console UI copy. Emily can you loop legal/security for the audit requirements?
Emily: will do. tagging @security to review classifier false-neg rate thresholds and retention acceptance.
policy-bot: policy checklist: data-classification, retention-limits, audit-traceability. Missing: embedding-PII handling detail.
Maggie L: thanks team — let's sync on Wed 9:30 for 30m. agenda: final config shape, console copy, rollout gating metrics. :thumbsup:
